body:
ChatGPT now shows ads. Over 100,000 advertisers have already used it, and OpenAI just expanded it to 26 more countries ("ChatGPT Ads expands to 26 new countries as over 100,000 advertisers have used the platform").

The part worth your attention isn't the expansion. It's what OpenAI said about how the ads get chosen — a system built to decide which ad fits what you're actually asking, not just what you clicked on before.

That's a different machine from Meta's. On Facebook and Instagram, you're bidding for attention — someone scrolling past a feed. On ChatGPT, you'd be showing up inside an answer someone asked for, while they're actively trying to solve a problem.

For a small business, that means the question changes. It's no longer "how do I stop the scroll." It's "would my product actually belong inside the answer to a question a stranger typed."

Most ad accounts aren't built to answer that yet. Worth sitting with before you're asked to spend on it.

slides.label: ADVERTISERS, 26 NEW COUNTRIES
slides.text: ChatGPT Ads just expanded, and over 100,000 advertisers have already used it.
Everyone will post this as news. The part worth checking is what kind of ad system this actually is.
On Meta, you buy attention from someone scrolling. That's a feed interruption, not a request.
On ChatGPT, the person typed a question first. The ad shows up inside their own search for an answer.
OpenAI built the ad stack around relevance to that question, not just your past clicks.
That changes what a 'good ad' even means. Interrupting well and answering well are not the same skill.
Most small business ad accounts are built only for the interrupt — a hook, a scroll-stop, a thumbnail.
None of that transfers automatically. A line that stops a scroll can fail completely inside an answer.

slides.label: THE CHECK
slides.text: Before you spend here, ask one thing: would my offer survive being read, not just seen?
The expansion is the headline. The shift from being seen to being asked for is the real news.
